questions.text: Autograd usually runs backward through a computation graph in:
At one operation, the gradient passed to a parent is:

options.a: upstream gradient times the local derivative
options.d: the learning rate divided by the batch size

questions.text: For z = x + y, the upstream gradient is routed to x and y as:

options.b: multiplied by x for y and y for x
options.d: the same upstream gradient to each input

questions.text: For z = x * y, the contribution to dL/dx is:

options.a: the upstream gradient divided by y

questions.text: Why do gradients accumulate at a node?

options.a: because every parameter must have the same gradient
options.b: because accumulation makes the forward pass faster
options.c: because a value can affect the loss through multiple downstream paths
options.d: because the loss is always linear
